title: Economy Guide
intro: General Age of Empires II economy principles. They are civ-agnostic — apply them, then layer your civilization's specific economy bonus (shown on each civ page). The single biggest skill: never let the Town Center sit idle.
principles: Never let the Town Center go idle — keep villagers training constantly from the first second.
Never get housed — build houses ahead of your population cap (check the count constantly).
Minimise villager walking time: every drop-off building (Mill, Lumber/Mining Camp, TC) should hug its resource.
Spend your resources — floating 1000 wood means 1000 wood of idle army/upgrades you didn't make.
Re-task idle villagers immediately; a standing villager is wasted economy.

sections.title: Food — Dark Age (sheep, boar, deer)
sections.body: Food drives your early up-time. Use the fastest sources first and never let villagers stand idle when one source runs out.
do: Keep sheep under the Town Center; eat one sheep fully before moving to the next so meat doesn't rot in two at once.

Lure both boars: send one villager to shoot the boar twice, then run back to the TC so it follows — garrison the villager if the boar is about to kill them. Lure around when your current food is ~half eaten.
Use deer: either drop a Mill near them or 'push' deer by tasking a few villagers to lure them toward your TC. Deer are fast food — don't waste them.
Berries last: they're slow, so they fill the gap after animals, often with a Mill + a few villagers.
dont: Don't let two food sources rot at once — only have one animal being eaten at a time per group.
Don't ignore the boar — it's a huge chunk of fast food and a common beginner mistake.
Don't forget shore fish on water/hybrid maps — they're free extra food early.

sections.title: Farming (how to farm)
sections.body: Farms are your long-term food. Build them around a Mill or Town Center and never let them expire.
do: Build farms adjacent to a Mill or Town Center so villagers drop off instantly — a ring of farms around the TC/Mill is standard.
Seed farms as wood allows; don't hoard wood while villagers sit idle on food.

Research Mill upgrades in age order — Horse Collar (Feudal), Heavy Plow (Castle, also +0.5 villager carry), Crop Rotation (Imperial). Each adds food per farm and pays back quickly once you have several farms.
Keep the farm reseed queue on, or re-task manually the instant a farm expires — an expired farm = idle villagers.
dont: Don't place farms far from a drop-off — walking wastes the food.
Don't skip the Mill upgrades when you run 6+ farms — the food-per-farm gain is one of the best investments in the game.
Don't let farms run out during a fight — re-balance before army clashes.

sections.title: Wood / chopping trees (how to chop)
sections.body: Wood funds farms, military buildings, archers and siege. Get a Lumber Camp on a real forest early.
do: First villagers can chop straggler trees near the TC, but build a Lumber Camp on the EDGE of a forest (nearest tile) as soon as you have ~60-100 wood.
Always place the Lumber Camp flush against the forest; keep villagers on the closest trees to the camp.
Research Double-Bit Axe (Feudal, faster wood) and Bow Saw (Castle, faster wood) — two big eco jumps.
Reposition the camp if villagers start a long walk; a fresh camp on a new forest beats a long trek.
dont: Don't chop stragglers all game — they run out and force walking; transition to a forest camp.
Don't float huge wood — convert surplus wood into farms, military, or a Market.
Don't forget to re-balance: if you're wood-starved mid-game, you under-invested in lumber early.

sections.title: Gold & Stone (mining)
sections.body: Gold funds age-ups, gold units and monks; stone funds Castles, Town Centers and towers.
do: Build a Mining Camp on the edge of the gold/stone pile so villagers walk minimally.
Research Gold Mining / Stone Mining (Feudal) and Gold/Stone Shaft Mining (Castle) for faster gathering.
Time stone for when you need Castles/TCs; time gold for age-ups and key units.
Relics and trade are long-term gold — grab relics with monks and set up trade on closed maps.
dont: Don't over-mine stone early unless you're turtling — it's usually lower priority than gold/wood/food.
Don't let the main gold pile run dry without a plan (relics/trade/secondary piles).

sections.title: Town Center & villager production
sections.body: Villager count is the foundation. Constant production and extra TCs win the macro game.
do: Train a villager every time the TC is free, all game — target 100+ villagers in long games.
In Castle Age build additional Town Centers (up to 3-4) to boom your economy.
Click age-ups at sensible villager counts (~22-28 for Feudal depending on strategy).
Use TC garrison to protect villagers from raids, then ungarrison to keep working.
dont: Don't delay the Feudal/Castle click excessively — idle TC time before an age-up still trains villagers, but dead time after is wasted.
Don't stop making villagers in Castle Age to 'save food' — that's where games are lost.

sections.title: Market
sections.body: The Market lets you rebalance resources and force timings; some civs (e.g. Saracens) get better rates.
do: Buy/sell to fix bottlenecks — e.g. sell wood/food to buy gold for an age-up or key unit.
Use it to hit a faster Castle/Imperial when your resource mix is off.
Build Trade Carts on closed/team maps for a renewable gold income in late game.
dont: Don't over-trade early — rates worsen as you buy/sell the same resource repeatedly.
Don't rely on the market for your main economy; it supplements, it doesn't replace villager income.

sections.title: Water & fishing economy (water / hybrid maps)
sections.body: On water and hybrid maps the sea is a second economy. Fishing ships convert wood into food and are often MORE wood-efficient than farms, so controlling the water snowballs your food income (source: t.me/kiritastrich).
do: Use Fish Traps (fishing ships) for long-term food on water: a 100-wood Fish Trap yields more food than a 60-wood farm AND you skip the Mill farm upgrades (Horse Collar / Heavy Plow / Crop Rotation) entirely.
If you WIN the water, keep making fishing ships — don't cap at ~10–12. Stopping early is a common way a hard-won water lead gets thrown away.
Gather shore fish and shallow food with villagers when it's close — villagers beat ships on shore fish; use the ships for deep-water fish, oysters and fish traps.
Prepare stone before a water game: extra Town Centers and a forward Dock/Castle lock in the lead (under-prepping stone cost the source player a decisive final).

On water maps Fast Castle is the whole game — and since Docks now fire 0 arrows in the Dark Age you can't shelter fishing ships under the Dock, so you must play Feudal (Galleys / Fire Ships) to defend them.
dont: Don't treat water as a side task — if your civ has a navy bonus (Longboats, Galleys, Fire/Demolition ships) the sea IS the game plan on water maps.
Don't assume a higher-rated opponent plays water — water is widely under-practiced, so a clean naval build can overwhelm stronger players.
Don't ignore the opponent's signature water unit — counter Longboats/Drakkars and galley masses with Fire Ships + Demolitions, never by abandoning the sea.

sections.title: Resource math & rates (from kiritastrich)
sections.body: Reason about gathering rates instead of guessing. Rate (food/s, wood/s) and idle time decide timings — not resource totals. Values below are approximate DE gathering rates per villager (fishing-ship rates per ship); civ bonuses stack on top.

notes: Farm distance constraint: keep farms TOUCHING the Town Center or Mill — the villager drops food off instantly at full rate. A farm 1–2 tiles from the drop-off loses food/s to walking, and a farm 3+ tiles out can gather 10–20% slower. Build a tight ring of farms; on a far food cluster, drop a new Mill instead of taking long walks.
Compute a farm's real food rate as (farm size − food left) ÷ seconds worked — the source channel measured ~105 food over 370 s ≈ 0.28 food/s on a base farm once walking is counted.
Fish traps are the most wood-efficient food on water: 100 wood of a fish trap yields more food than 60 wood of a farm, and you skip all three Mill farm upgrades.
When benchmarking your own replays, exclude the last farm in a batch — an about-to-expire farm skews the per-farm average.
